newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $64.00, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $64.00, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $64.00 by major packers was up $1.00 from last week's sales, but passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00, feedlot sources said.
"A bid at $65.00 would buy all the cattle they need," said a Texas Panhandle-area manager.
Fed cattle prices were supported by sharply higher beef prices on Monday and outlooks for continued strength this week, the sources said.
Beef price advances were powered by tight supplies and retail demand for Independence Day featuring, they said.

Beef stocks were tight following brisk sales the past two weeks which lowered packer inventories, sources said. Closing boxed beef prices on Monday rose $1.58 to $1.82 per cwt, with 142 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Strength in fed cattle prices also was tied to gains in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures, they said.

Projections for higher fed cattle sales also were fueled by trade in Nebraska late Monday at $105.00 per cwt on a dressed basis, up $2.00 from last week's top price and equivalent to $65.00 on a live basis, several sources said.
